messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran into weird auth bridge behavior when a projectless key is used to call /v1/generate. it attributes to org but console consent flow doesn't show the linked project. anyone seen this?
jonah: can you paste the request headers? maybe missing X-Project-Id or origin header
maria: sample request:
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer sk_org_123
X-User-Consent: consent_id=abc
```
jonah: hmm the bridge should exchange org token -> project claim if projectless fallback exists. is the exchange service returning project_id in the response?
kevin: looking at exchange logs now — service returns 204 with no body when consent param present. seems consent middleware short-circuits before attaching project claim.
sasha: is that the expected behavior for org-wide consents? console expects a project to be attached so we can show per-project SLOs and quota breakdowns.
maria: exactly. current behavior causes console to show "org-level" attribution and no per-project metrics, which confuses customers and breaks quota budgeting.
jonah: proposal: exchange service should attach a synthetic project id (e.g., org-default-<org>) when consent is org-level and there is no explicit project. also emit telemetry flag synthetic_project=true so downstream systems know it's synthetic.
kevin: +1 for telemetry flag. but billing pipeline treats project ids specially. we'll need mapping in billing so synthetic projects don't create orphan invoices.
sasha: alternatively we could return an X-Project-Override header from the exchange and punt the mapping to downstream services (console, billing). less server-side magic.
maria: downside of header approach: every downstream service must adopt it which is a lot of churn. prefer server-side mapping with an explicit opt-out for orgs that want the old behavior.
kevin: quick workable change: exchange adds header in response: X-Assigned-Project: org-default-1766123450 and increments metric auth.exchange.assigned_project{synthetic=true}. fallback toggle behind flag.
sasha: add console feature-flag to hide synthetic projects in the project picker for orgs with flat-billing. also record original_token_type (org_key|sa_key|project_key) and consent_scope in telemetry.
maria: agreed. I'll draft RFC and include the telemetry schema. we should gate on a feature flag auth-bridge.synthetic-project and canary in a single org first.
jonah: creating PR now. @kevin can you add unit tests for header behavior and an e2e that checks quota attribution?
kevin: will do. testing plan: unit for header + metric, e2e where console receives X-Assigned-Project and surfaces per-route quota. also add regression ensuring billing mapping ignores synthetic marker.
sasha: one more note — don't forget to preserve original token metadata in logs so we can trace back to org-level consent when support triages. add fields original_token_type and consent_id to auth logs.
maria: good call. i'll include that in the RFC.
jonah: PR link in a sec, will tag deploy-bot for canary deploy.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary env, ref=pr/3125, flags: auth-bridge.synthetic-project=false
kevin: will split PR into exchange change + billing mapping + console display, to keep reviews small.
sasha: make sure telemetry fields are in the common schema (trace_id, original_token_type, consent_scope, synthetic_project).
maria: RFC created: https://go/repo/ISSUE-512 — includes UX sketches for console indicator "Synthetic project (org default)" and telemetry table.
jonah: pinged infra to reserve canary org for tests.
kevin: LGTM on tests, starting work.
sasha: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary deployed at 1766123475
